sentences.text: These appeals has arisen from the common judgment.
Hence, these appeals are disposed of analogously.

3. In nutshell, the prosecution case before the Trial Court was that on 19.04.2017 at 07:00 pm,
Phool Singh (PW-2) alongwith Rohan (PW-4) and Shivali Jha (PW-1) on motorcycle were going from Pipariya to Pachmarhi.
On two motorcycles, the appellants and one delinquent juvenile came there and stopped them then they started abusing and beating the victim by hands and fists.
The appellant-Shibbu fired on Phool Singh (PW-2).
He suffered the gunshot injury in his right thigh.
After that, all the four persons went towards Pachmarhi.
The Police was called by dialing 100 number but they did not reach on the time in the forest ranger.

They were brought to Hospital,
Pipariya where on information, A.S.I. Rajkumar Shakya (PW-6) went and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:5193 3 CRA-4170-2021 recorded the Dehati Nalishi on statement of Phool Singh (PW-2).
The victim Phool Singh (PW-2) was medically examined.
The pant of the victim Phool Singh was seized from the possession of the Medical Officer.
Spot map was prepared.
Caste certificate of Shivali Jha was received and seized.
Blank cartridge was recovered.

After investigation,
the charge sheet was filed against the three persons and against the one assailant, the charge sheet was submitted before Special Judge, SC & ST (POA) Act, Hoshangabad.

4. The Trial Court framed the charges under Sections 341, 323 (on 3 counts in alternate), 323/34,
307 of IPC and Section 3(2)(V) of SC & ST (POA) Act, 1989 against the appellant Shibbu and additional charges under Section 201 of IPC and Section 25(1B)(b) and Section 27(1) of Arms Act were also framed.
The appellants abjured the guilt and prayed for trial.
5. The prosecution examined the seven witnesses and the Trial Court also examined the appellants.
The appellants had taken the defence that they have falsely been implicated in the case.

The appellant-Javed Mota had also taken specific defence that on the date of the incident, he was working in the Official Mess of Army, Pachmarhi and he had examined Hawaldar Sunil Kumar Singh (DW-1).
6. The Trial Court, after hearing the parties, passed the impugned judgment.

The Trial Court has acquitted all the accused persons for the offence punishable under Section 3(2)(V) of SC & ST (POA)
Act and also acquitted the appellant Shibbu @ Shivkumar under Section 25(1B)(b) and Section 27(1)
of Arms Act and convicted and sentenced as stated in para no.1 of the impugned judgment.

Hence,
these appeals are filed.

sentences.text: 8. Learned counsel for the appellant further submitted that Phool Singh (PW-2) has clearly stated that appellants-Monu and Javed were not saying anything and has also admitted that during the incident, they had not assaulted to anyone.
Only Shibbu and Nikil were talking with Shivali Jha (PW-1).
This witness has also admitted in the cross-examination that there is enmity between Shibbu and family of Dashrath Jha (the husband of Shivali Jha).
In para-25 of the cross-examination, Phool Singh has clearly admitted that Monu Rai and Javed Mota had neither assaulted nor abused to him.
Rohan (PW-4) has not identified that these appellants were present on the spot.
Looking to the facts and circumstances, the appellants has wrongly been convicted by the Trial Court.
Hence, the appeal be allowed and appellant be acquitted from the aforesaid charges.

9. Shri Narendra Nikhare, learned counsel for the appellants Shibbu and Javed Mota has submitted that Javed Mota was not present on the spot NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:5193 5 CRA-4170-2021 and his name does not find place in Dehati Nalishi (Ex.P-3) and instead of his name, the name of one Rashid Mota is written in Ex.P-3.

On 30.06.2017, the name of this appellant Javed Mota was impleaded by filing Ex.P-4 and statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
(Ex.P-7).
From the defence witness, it has been proved by that Javed Mota was working in the Army Mess at Pachmarhi.
On the date of the incident i.e. 19.04.2017, he was working in the Army Mess from 12:00 pm to 10:00 pm.
By document (Ex.D-3), this fact has been proved that he has not assigned any role in the offence.
Thus, his name has falsely been impleaded in the case.
Nothing has been recovered from the possession.
The injured has also not stated that Javed Mota had not inflicted any injury to him.
10. Learned counsel for the appellant has further submitted that the victim suffered a gunshot injury in thigh and fire was not repeated.
There was enmity between the family of Shivali Jha (PW-1) and the appellant- Shibbu.
Dr. Sunil Nagar (PW-3) has clearly stated that the charring and blackening was found in the injury.
There was no fracture in the thigh bone and the injury may be self-inflicted.
On that basis, it is submitted that the injury was self-inflicted to implicate the appellant as Shivali Jha's husband was a criminal person and he was facing multiple criminal cases.

14. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
15.
The witness Phool Singh (PW-2) has stated that he identified the accused persons in April, 2017 at 7:00-7:30 pm.
This witness alongwith Shivali Jha (PW-1) and Rohan (PW-4) were returning from SDOP Office, Pipariya to Pachmarhi.
When they were on the way to Pachmarhi on motorcycle, four persons came there on two motorcycles.
On one motorcycle, there were Shibbu and Nikhil and another motorcycle, there were Javed Mota and Monu Rai.
They came behind the motorcycles and started abusing and said them to stop the motorcycle.
When he stopped the accused Shibbu and Nikhil said to Shivali Jha that she asked her husband to compromise the matter.
Monu Rai and Javed Mota were not saying much.
This fact has been supported by Shivali Jha (PW-1) when she was returning alongwith Phool Singh and Rohan on a motorcycle.
On two motorcycles, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:5193 7 CRA-4170-2021 four persons came there and stopped them and started abusing.
Shibbu Noriya said that don't involve in the matter of Courts.
Shibbu pushed him and was abusing her.
16. The witnesses Phool Singh (PW-2) and Shivali Jha (PW-1) had stated that Shibbu fired on Phool Singh by a pistol.
Phool Singh suffered the injury and dialed 100 number.
In the intervening time, a vehicle of Forest Department came there.

From that vehicle, they came to Government Hospital,
Pipariya.
Rohan suffered abrasion and Phool Singh suffered the gunshot injury.
17. Witness Rohan (PW-4) has also supported the fact that when they were returning on a motorcycle from SDOP Office, Pipariya to Pachmarhi alongwith Shivali Jha and Phool Singh.
When they reached Richera turn, four persons came there on two motorcycle.
The assailants wrapped their face by cloths and started assaulting them with hands and fists.
They also fired on Phool Singh.
By that, he suffered the injury in his leg.
Shivali Jha (PW-1) was only pushed.
He has not identified any accused persons.
Thus, all the three persons had supported that when they were returning on a motorcycle, four persons on two motorcycles came there and obstructed them.
Then, four persons abused them and started beating them by hands and fists.
One accused person fired arm on Phool Singh (PW-2) by which he suffered the injury in his thigh.
18. Dr. Sunil Nagar (PW-3) had clearly stated that on 19.04.2017, he was posted at Community Health Centre, Pipariya as a Medical Officer.

The victim Phool Singh s/o Deendayal Katiya aged about 27 years was brought NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:5193 8 CRA-4170-2021 by Constable Yashpal Batch No.376 from Police Station Pipariya at 08.40 pm.

Heexamined the victim and found a gunshot entry wound circular lacerated posterior medially side of lower 1/3 of right thigh measuring 1x1 cm margins were inverted and blackening, tattooing all around the wound direction forward end medially and also found an exit wound circular lacerated wound medial side of middle 1/3 of right thigh measuring 1x1 cm margins everted.
He has opined that the gunshot injury was within 2 to 6 hours from the time of examination.

He has further submitted that on the pant of injured, two black colored torn parts were found whose area was 6.5x1 cm and second 1x1 Monu Rai vs The State Of M.P. on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61159179/

19. This witness had admitted that there was no fracture in the bone and has also stated that the injury may be self-inflicted and if a person fires from the distance then blackening and tattooing will not appear and also admitted that thigh is not a vital organ.
20. Thus, this fact is supported that in the incident, the assailants had beaten the injured Shivali Jha (PW-1), Phool Singh (PW-2) and Rohan (PW- 4) by hands and fists.
One of them assaulted the injured Phool Singh by gunshot injury.
21. On the point of the role of appellants, it is worth mentioned that Shivali Jha (PW-1) has clearly stated that she by face and name can identify Shibbu and Nikhil.
She has not identified the rest of the two accused persons.
She knows the appellants Monu Rai and Javed Mota due to their names.
In para no.26 of the cross-examination, she has clearly admitted that the Police NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:5193 9 CRA-4170-2021 had not made identification parade regarding Javed and Monu.
She is stating the names of Javed and Monu on the basis that Phool Singh (PW-2) told their names.
On that basis, she told their names to Police.
22. Witness Rohan (PW-4) has not identified any accused person.
He is stating that all the accused persons wrapped their face by cloth.
23. On the statement of Phool Singh (PW-2), the Dehati Nalishi (Ex.P- 2) was lodged.
There is no mention about the name of Javed Mota.
In place of Javed Mota, the name of Rashid Mota has been mentioned.
From the document (Ex.P-4), it is also clearly stated that by mistake, he told the name of Rashid Mota and Javed Mota was involved.
This application was filed to Police Officer.
After two months and 11 days on 30.06.2017, when the Dehati Nalishi (Ex.P-3) was recorded.
24. In the light of the statement of Shivali Jha (PW-1) who is the injured and was present on the spot. She has not identified these two persons Javed Mota and Monu Rai.
She has stated their names only on the basis that Phool Singh (PW-2) told their names.
25. Phool Singh (PW-2) in his cross-examination has clearly stated that appellants Javed Mota and Monu Rai were not stating anything.

He has stated that from the very beginning,
he has mentioned the name of Javed Mota.
It was not the situation that he was unconscious and due to nervousness, he has named Rashid Mota in place of Javed Mota.

sentences.text: In para no.24 of the cross-examination, the witness Phool Singh (PW-2) has clearly admitted that Monu and Javed had not abused him.
Thus, regarding the role of Javed Mota, the prosecution case becomes doubtful as in Dehati Nalishi , his name was not mentioned instead of this appellant and the name of one Rashid Mota was stated.
This application was filed after a long delay and only on the basis of statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., the statements were recorded on 01.07.2017.
He has been implicated in the aforesaid offence.

27. The Investigating Officer recorded the statement of Phool Singh on 01.05.2017 but he has told that in the statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., Phool Singh (PW-2) has stated the name of Javed Mota as a assailant.
He has also stated that he cannot tell whether on the date of incident, Javed Mota was not present on the spot and was working in Army Mess, Pachmarhi.

Thus,
the Investigating Officer himself has not verified the fact that Javed was present on the spot or not?
It was the duty of the Investigating Officer.
Only on the basis that three interested witnesses told his name, therefore, he is implicated in the offence.
28. Furthermore, Phool Singh (PW-2) has never stated that the appellants Javed Mota and Monu Rai were present to guard the incident.
29. It is also clear that Shivali Jha (PW-1) had stated that she did not identify Monu Rai and no active role has been assigned to Monu Rai.
In these circumstances, the appellants Monu Rai and Javed Mota are entitled for the benefit of doubt.

Hence, giving benefit of doubt, they are acquitted from NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:5193 11 CRA-4170-2021 all the aforesaid charges and their conviction under Sections 307/34, 341 and 323 of IPC are set aside.
As a result, their sentence is also quashed.

30. Regarding the role of appellant-Shibbu @ Shivkumar Noriya, the witness Phool Singh has clearly stated that Shibbu alongwith Nikhil (the delinquent juvenile) assaulted him and Shibbu fired at him and he suffered injuries.
This witness has also tried to improve the fact that the assault was in his chest but due to shot by Nikhil and Shibbu, he suffered the injury on thigh.
31. Shivali Jha (PW-1) has clearly stated that Shibbu shot the injured Phool Singh by Pistol and the witness Rohan has also stated that one of the assailant assaulted the victim by Tamancha.
As a result, injured Phool Singh suffered the injury in his thigh.
This injury is supported by the prosecution witnesses.
32. The witness Phool Singh (PW-2) in his cross-examination has clearly stated that the injury by the firearms was caused from the close range.
In para no.19 of his cross-examination, he has clearly stated that the appellant Shibbu fired on his leg from the close range and denied the suggestion that he himself has caused the injury.
33. Though, in this case, the Investigating Officer has failed to produce the firearm and it is alleged that the firearm was thrown by the appellant in Denwa river.
In search, the firearm was not found as per Search Panchnama (Ex.P-24).

sentences.text: Thus, only on the basis that the firearm was not recovered.
The appellant is not entitled for acquittal.
From the statement of eye-witness, it is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:5193 12 CRA-4170-2021 clear that the appellant Shibbu @ Shivkumar had assaulted the victim by gunshot.
On the point of the self-inflicted injury, the witness Phool Singh has clearly stated that the firearm was made from the close range.
In that situation, the blackening and tattooing were found.
The injury was of such a name that the bullet entered from the one side and came out from the other side.

Looking to the evidence of the other witnesses and Dehati Nalishi (Ex.P-3) at the time of the injury as stated by Medical Officer Dr. Sunil Nagar (PW-3), it cannot be inferred any how the injured himself caused the injury to implicate the accused persons.
35. From the perusal of the injury, in this case, the injury was caused in the thigh.
Thigh is not a vital organ but weapon used in the offence was the firearm.
Injury was a such nature that the bullet crossed the whole thigh.
It may be in hurry/nervousness and interference of the other persons that the appellant caused the injury to the victim in thigh but use of firearm was the intention of the victim.
In the case of Shiv Kumar Singh (supra) one firearm was made from 12 bore gun and the pellets were found in the body of the victim and that was such a nature that only simple injury was caused.
The quarrel started with the other persons that were not the injured.

In that circumstances,
this Court has held that no mens rea was caused to the injury to the victim.
36. In the case of Shyam Sharma (supra) , there is no mention of how much injury caused and what was the nature of the injury.
It is also stated that without premeditation, the injury was caused and that was not a vital part of the body.

Hence, the accused persons were convicted for the offence NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:5193 13 CRA-4170-2021 punishable under Section 324 of IPC.
37.

In this case, it is clear that there was enmity between the husband of Shivali Jha (PW-1) and Phool Singh (PW-2) was working in their home and Shivali Jha (PW-1) was treating him as her brother-in-law.
The appellant alongwith other persons caused wrongful restrain and assaulted the accompanying persons and shot the firearm on Phool Singh (PW-2).
Thus, the incident was premeditated and well-planned.
In these circumstances, looking to the nature of the injury, the appellant is not entitled for the benefit at the principle of the aforesaid case.
In that situation, it cannot be held that the appellant was not having the intention to cause the injury or death to the injured.

38. Looking to the above facts and circumstances, the conviction of the appellant Shibbu @
Shivkumar Noriya is affirmed.
39. The Trial Court has sentenced the appellant for 10 years of rigorous imprisonment for the offence punishable under Section 307 of IPC.
It appears to be too harsh in proportion to injury suffered by the victim.
Hence, his jail sentence under Section 307 of IPC is reduced to seven years of rigorous imprisonment.
Hence, the appellant Shibbu @ Shivkumar Noriya i s partially allowed and his conviction for the offence punishable under Section 307, 341, 323 (on two counts) and 201 of IPC is sustained.

Rest of the sentence of the appellant i.e. under Section 341, 323 and 201 of IPC as imposed by the Trial Court is affirmed but his sentence for the offence punishable under Section 307 Monu Rai vs The State Of M.P. on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61159179/
7 of IPC is modified.
He shall suffer 07 years of rigorous imprisonment in place of 10 years of rigorous imprisonment.

40. The appeals of the appellants-Javed Mota @ Iliyas Khan and Monu Rai is allowed.
Both appellants are acquitted from all the aforesaid charges.
The bail bonds of the appellants are discharged.
The fine amount if any deposited before the Trial Court be refunded to the appellants.
41. Thus, with the above conclusion and direction, these appeals are disposed of.
42. With the copy of judgment, the record of the trial Court be returned back for information and necessary action.
43. Record of these appeals be consigned to the record room.

The appellant is not entitled for acquittal.
The injury was of such a name that the bullet entered from the one side and came out from the other side.
Looking to the evidence of the other witnesses and Dehati Nalishi (Ex.P-3) at the time of the injury as stated by Medical Officer Dr. Sunil Nagar (PW-3), it cannot be inferred any how the injured himself caused the injury to implicate the accused persons.
35. From the perusal of the injury, in this case, the injury was caused in the thigh.
Thigh is not a vital organ but weapon used in the offence was the firearm.
Injury was a such nature that the bullet crossed the whole thigh.
It may be in hurry/nervousness and interference of the other persons that the appellant caused the injury to the victim in thigh but use of firearm was the intention of the victim.
Hence, the accused persons were convicted for the offence NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:5193 13 CRA-4170-2021 punishable under Section 324 of IPC.
37.
In this case, it is clear that there was enmity between the husband of Shivali Jha (PW-1) and Phool Singh (PW-2) was working in their home and Shivali Jha (PW-1) was treating him as her brother-in-law.
The appellant alongwith other persons caused wrongful restrain and assaulted the accompanying persons and shot the firearm on Phool Singh (PW-2).
Thus, the incident was premeditated and well-planned.
In these circumstances, looking to the nature of the injury, the appellant is not entitled for the benefit at the principle of the aforesaid case.
In that situation, it cannot be held that the appellant was not having the intention to cause the injury or death to the injured.
It appears to be too harsh in proportion to injury suffered by the victim.
